name: Weighted Dips
grip: Neutral grip with palms facing inward, grasping parallel bars firmly with wrists stacked over forearms.
description: Lower and press your bodyweight with added external plate resistance suspended from a dipping belt on parallel bars, developing pressing power in the triceps and chest.
setup: Secure a dipping belt around your waist with the desired weight plate suspended comfortably between your legs.
Mount parallel dip bars with arms fully extended, shoulders depressed away from your ears, and elbows softly unlocked.
Incline your torso slightly forward (~15 degrees) with knees bent and feet crossed behind or held steady beneath you.
instructions: Lower your body under control by bending your elbows and allowing shoulders to extend until upper arms are at least parallel to the floor (elbows at 90 degrees).
Maintain the slight forward torso tilt to protect the anterior shoulder capsule and engage the chest.
Push forcefully through your palms into the bars to extend your arms, driving your body back to the top lockout.
Do not bounce aggressively out of the bottom position; reverse smoothly under muscular tension.
cues: Keep shoulders packed down away from ears.
Maintain a slight forward lean throughout.
Drive through the heels of the hands.
commonMistakes: Descending too deep into uncontrolled hyperextension, placing extreme strain on anterior shoulder joint.
Swinging the suspended weight plates or kicking the legs to generate momentum.
Shrugging shoulders up toward the ears at the lockout.

logging.example: One 20 kg plate on dipping belt: record 20 kg added external load.
logging.note: Record only the external added plate mass on the dip belt; athlete bodyweight provides the baseline load.

variantNote: Parallel bar dip performed with additional external weight suspended from a dip belt. Emphasizes triceps and lower chest.
